blocks.html:
This method executes a giuven asynchronous job with a lock on the given keys. You can optionally pass a 
provider name to be used for locking. If no provider is passed, the default provider (in-memory or the 
provider configuerd in `medusa-config.ts`) will be used.

types.name: T
types.description: The type of the job's result.

types.name: keys
types.description: The keys to lock durng the job's execution.

types.name: job
types.description: The asynchronous job to execute while the keys are locked.

types.name: args
types.description: Additional arguments for the job execution.

children.name: timeout
children.description:
The timeout (in seconds) for acquiring the lock. If the time out is passed, the job is canceled and the lock is released.
Its value defaults to `5` seconds if no value is passed or if you pass a value less than `1`.

children.name: provider
children.description: The provider name to use for locking. If no provider is passed, the default provider (in-memory or the provider configuerd in `medusa-config.ts`) will be used.

types.name: sharedContext
types.description: A context used to share resources, such as transaction manager, between the application and the module.

children.name: transactionManager
children.description: An instance of a transaction manager of type `TManager`, which is a typed parameter passed to the context to specify the type of the `transactionManager`.

children.name: manager
children.description: An instance of a manager, typically an entity manager, of type `TManager`, which is a typed parameter passed to the context to specify the type of the `manager`.

children.name: isolationLevel
children.description: A string indicating the isolation level of the context. Possible values are `READ UNCOMMITTED`, `READ COMMITTED`, `REPEATABLE READ`, or `SERIALIZABLE`.

children.name: enableNestedTransactions
children.description: A boolean value indicating whether nested transactions are enabled.

children.name: eventGroupId
children.description: A string indicating the ID of the group to aggregate the events to be emitted at a later point.

children.name: transactionId
children.description: A string indicating the ID of the current transaction.

children.name: runId
children.description: A string indicating the ID of the current run.

children.name: messageAggregator
children.description: An instance of a message aggregator, which is used to aggregate messages to be emitted at a later point.

children.name: requestId
children.description: A string indicating the ID of the current request.

children.name: idempotencyKey
children.description: A string indicating the idempotencyKey of the current workflow execution.

children.name: parentStepIdempotencyKey
children.description: A string indicating the idempotencyKey of the parent workflow execution.

children.name: preventReleaseEvents
children.description: preventReleaseEvents

children.name: isCancelling
children.description: A boolean value indicating whether the current workflow execution is being cancelled.

children.name: cancelingFromParentStep
children.description:
Weither or not a sub workflow cancellation is being triggered from a parent step.
If true, the parent step will not be triggered by the sub workflow.

types.name: Promise
types.description: The result of the job execution.

blocks.html:
This method acquires a lock on the given keys. You can optionally pass a provider name to be used for locking. 
If no provider is passed, the default provider (in-memory or the provider configuerd in `medusa-config.ts`) will be used.

You can pass an owner for the lock, which limits who can extend or release the acquired lock. Then, if you use this method again
passing the same owner, the lock's expiration time is extended with the value passed in the `expire` argument. Otherwise, if you pass a
different owner, the method throws an error.

For example, to acquire a lock on a product with ID `prod_123` for a user with ID `user_123`:

```ts
await lockingModuleService.acquire("prod_123", {
  ownerId: "user_123",
  expire: 60
})
```

In this example, you acquire a lock on the product with ID `prod_123` for the user with ID `user_123`. You extend the 
lock's expiration time by `60` seconds.

To specify the provider to use for locking, you can pass the provider name in the `args` argument:

```ts
await lockingModuleService.acquire("prod_123", {
  ownerId: "user_123",
  expire: 60,
  provider: "lp_my-lock"
})
```

types.description: The keys to acquire the lock on.

types.name: args
types.description: Additional arguments for acquiring the lock.

children.name: ownerId
children.description: The owner ID for the lock. If specified, only the owner can release the lock or extend its expiration time.

children.name: expire
children.description:
The expiration time (in seconds) for the lock. If the lock is already acquired and the owner is the same, the expiration time is extended
by the value passed. If not specified, the lock does not expire.

children.name: provider
children.description: The provider name to use for locking. If no provider is passed, the default provider (in-memory or the provider configuerd in `medusa-config.ts`) will be used.

blocks.html:
This method releases a lock on the given keys. You can optionally pass a provider name to be used for locking.
If no provider is passed, the default provider (in-memory or the provider configuerd in `medusa-config.ts`) will be used.

If the lock has an owner, you must pass the same owner to release the lock.

For example, to release a lock on a product with ID `prod_123` for a user with ID `user_123`:

```ts
await lockingModuleService.release("prod_123", {
  ownerId: "user_123"
})
```

In this example, you release the lock on the product with ID `prod_123` for the user with ID `user_123`.

To specify the provider to use for locking, you can pass the provider name in the `args` argument:

```ts
await lockingModuleService.release("prod_123", {
  ownerId: "user_123",
  provider: "lp_my-lock"
})
```

types.name: keys
types.description: The keys to release the lock from.

types.name: args
types.description: Additional arguments for releasing the lock.

children.name: ownerId
children.description:
The ID of the lock's owner. The lock can be released either if it doesn't have an owner, or 
if its owner ID matches the one passed in this property.

children.name: provider
children.description: The provider name to use for locking. If no provider is passed, the default provider (in-memory or the provider configuerd in `medusa-config.ts`) will be used.

blocks.html:
This method releases all locks. If you specify an owner ID, then all locks that the owner has acquired are released.

You can also pass a provider name to be used for locking. If no provider is passed, the default provider (in-memory or the provider configuerd in `medusa-config.ts`) will be used.

For example, to release all locks for a user with ID `user_123`:

```ts
await lockingModuleService.releaseAll({
  ownerId: "user_123"
})
```

In this example, you release all locks for the user with ID `user_123`.

To specify the provider to use for locking, you can pass the provider name in the `args` argument:

```ts
await lockingModuleService.releaseAll({
  ownerId: "user_123",
  provider: "lp_my-lock"
})
```

types.description: Additional arguments for releasing the locks.

children.name: ownerId
children.description: The ID of a lock owner. If specified, all locks that the owner has acquired are released.

children.name: provider
